title: Great value for a soft tactical rifle case
text:
I picked one of these up at a local survival store and was amazed at the features and craftsmanship for the price paid. Comparing this to my [[ASIN:B002ECR4JC 5.11 Tactical 36" Gun Case]], I would say that the fit and finish is just a hair under 5.11. That said, the Drago soft case affords in my opinion, a better feature set than the 5.11 for about half the cost.

From Drago's website ([...]):

(It's a shame the Drago does not post a more detailed product description and pictures of all of their case features)

PRODUCT FEATURES
-Padded backpack straps for hands-free transport
-Three large storage pouches for ammunition and firearm accessories
-Dual zippered storage area
-Designed to protect a rifle during transport and storage
-Made of 600D Polyester
-Dimensions: 36"x14"x10"

Features 5.11 has that Drago does not:

-Shoulder carry strap
-Two horizontal rows of MOLLE webbing (with four included Velcro straps) for securing weapon(s) (Condor has two vertical Velcro straps for strapping in weapon)
-Three outside name/tag/patch Velcro attachment points (Condor has one morale badge sized one on the front)
-Lockable YKK zippers
-1,050-denier nylon (Drago has 600D Polyester)

Features that Drago has that 5.11 does not:

-Two small zippered compartments on outside front of case (securing small items such as wallet and keys).
-Three Velcro + quick-release buckle divided compartments that will hold at least 6 30rd AR magazines. These alone add $45 to the 5.11 Tactical Case price (if you want to equip it similarly to the Drago).
-Two large zippered compartments inside middle storage area (between the main rifle case compartment and the magazine compartments).
-Backpack style straps on back of case for hands-free transport.

I think the only thing Drago should really change about this case is adding lockable zippers with the extra metal loops so that you can lock it down to keep the kids out. Maybe they could add a shoulder strap (the Drago has built-in attachment points for one). You can always loosen the topmost backpack strap and use it for single shoulder carry. Overall, for roughly half the price of a "big name" soft case, you can purchase a Drago and avail yourself to more built-in storage space. If the zippers hold up, I will only be purchasing Drago soft cases from now on.

title: Tried 3 different brands, and Legit Camping was my favorite.
text:
[[VIDEOID:68e2b67e7fa9b61f4344b9d3523a356c]] [[VIDEOID:476bc1412a5685e90d74cbc3899edcad]] [[VIDEOID:9a1051fbb9f86c3600ebc8a4fe64dc9c]] [[VIDEOID:fa11bfb0e067fff29a1a8177f73a9349]] This is my 3rd type of camping/backpacking hammock (both the top sellers on Amazon), and all I can say that the Legit Camping Hammock is my favorite of all three. Couple items I wanted to note:
- The straps are a little short. I tried to get them around a thick tree which made them too short to reach my hammock between the two trees. I ended up using some webbing I had to make the distance. Not a huge deal. If you want, just untie the knots, and make the rope much longer.
- The straps have the covers that widen the load and don't wreck trees or posts. This is very important when selecting a hammock. I don't know of any others that do it the way legit camping does.
- The main body of the hammock is wide enough so that the stitching does not go behind your back. I've used two others that do to a small width have the stitching behind you and it makes for a very uncomfortable sleep. This hammock is wide enough that it is not a problem.
- I am 6'6" & 250+ pounds and there is more than enough room for me to lay down and no worries about fabric stretching or ripping. I have put myself and my wife in the hammock without any problems at all.
- The carabiners are a little more high end than other brands.
- I spent 3 nights at scout camp on this hammock and slept perfectly. I was worried about arching too much, but heard laying diagonal allows you to sleep flat. Because this hammock is so wide, it will allow you to sleep diagonal unlike the smaller hammocks you find online.

Overall, I loved it so much I bought a second. I made a short video on my experience because I loved it so much.

Overall, I am happy with this lounger. Its strong and held up with my two boys. Its comfortable, on a windy day, easy to inflate and fun for my family.

title: Great Home Gym, Doesn't Require Much Room
text: I previously had a weight bench with a variety of barbells and dumbbells. However, with a growing family and all of the clutter that comes along with it, space started to become a premium in our house. This home gym appeared to be the perfect solution to get a variety of full body exercises without sacrifice a large area of your home. It only takes up about an 7' by 7' area, but requires about a 10' by 9' area in order to comfortably workout. The product comes packaged extremely well by the company and miraculously survived the beating it took during its journey. The assembly wasn't too bad and I was able to easily complete it by myself in about 3 hours. The one issue I had with assembly came when I got to the very end. All of the sudden the instructions seem to just end and you're left there with a pile of straps, bars, and hand grips. They don't explain where or how they're supposed to be attached. So I had to look at the various exercises to see how they should be arranged on the machine. It would have been nice to include this in the instruction manual. The entire gym is well-made with heavy-duty steel that gives the impression it will last for many years to come. It's fairly easy to switch the attachments and power rods in order to do the different exercises. It will take a little getting used to before you figure out exactly which cables attach to the different parts of the machine, but eventually it becomes second nature. The power rods that come with the product go up to 210 lbs, which I would imagine is sufficient for most people including myself. But if you're looking to become a total musclehead, it says it's upgradeable to 310 and 410 lbs with additional purchases. The power rods to kind of flop around and wiggle in the cradle they come in. You can purchase the power rod rejuvenator for about $15, but I'm not sure why they wouldn't include such a cheap part with the gym to begin with. It's also easily adjustable to different people's heights, which is useful when different people are using the same machine. Overall I'm extremely pleased with both the quality of the gym and the variety of workouts you can get for such a small amount of space.

title: The Porsche or Tesla of electric bikes!
text:
After three months of use, I've found there are several things that put the Elby at the top of any list of recommended e-bikes.

- It's purpose built so that everything is smoothly integrated into a beautiful package. Almost all cables and wiring are enclosed protected from the weather and getting snagged on obstacles. The integrated control system functions smoothly and perfectly and it provides the rider with a wide variety of information.
- It's superior BionX motor is unique in design delivering super-powerful performance while being stealthily quiet (you will be astounded at how quietly it operates and learn to use the built-in bell frequently so you don't surprise folks). It handles the steep hills around my house in the Oakland Hills and on the trails like a champ and doesn't have the whine or noise I've come to associate with other e-bikes. This is a big deal for me.
- It's battery has great capacity which coupled with the BionX motor gives it great range.
- It's well balanced and easy to ride with little flex and great directional stability. It corners like a champ.
- Assembly is a snap and took me less than five minutes.

You can use it like a moped and completely rely on the electric motor to get you up to speed... or choose one of a variety of assist levels to get the exercise you desire.

It's setup makes it easy to charge the battery either on or off the bike.

The built in rack supports on the back frame are perfect for holding panniers. I suggest the Ibera Bicycle Bag PakRak Clip-On Quick-Release All Weather Bike Panniers (Pair), Includes Rain Cover.

It's hydraulic brakes are amazingly strong and functional compared to traditional bike brakes. This is also a big deal for me.

All in all, while it is not the cheapest of e-bikes, it is the best IMHO!

Cons-
- cost
- weight (it comes in at about 57 pounds) so you can't use a standard strap-on bike rack. I suggest the Saris Freedom EX 2-Bicycle Universal Hitch Rack.

title: Get the Rogue R3 if you can afford it, otherwise get this.
text:
I'm typing this on my phone so it's a little choppy and may lack coherence, but here are my thoughts. I'm 35 and haven't lifted consistently for over 10 years but bought this rack for my new house so that I can do Stronglifts 5x5 in the comfort of my home. I just bought a 15/16" wrench last night to properly tighten down all the bolts (the nuts/bolts on this thing are way bigger than I realized) and got all the plywood to build a lifting platform which I also plan to bolt this rack onto (plans from Iron Mind using plywood and horse stall mats from Tractor Supply Company).

For lots of discussion, check out a thread called "HD Titan Power Rack 2x3" at bodybuilding DOT com, but pay far more attention to reviews from December 2014 or newer; it appears that there were some kinks with earlier models that got worked out with the newer batches. Specifically, I had no rust on mine and the pin/pipe safeties are now identical to those found on the Rogue R3 (no more "washers" welded into the ends). The plastic on the J hooks is still cheap, but as mentioned in that thread, you can purchase some better stuff on eBay for under $20.

For a detailed and fair video, check out YouTube for a video called "Titan HD Power Rack vs. Rogue R3 Power Rack (Detailed Comparison)" from user thesergeant. title: Better than you’d expect.
text: So, after doing a ton of research I was able to conclude that this is for sure the best single wheel driven electric bike you can get for the price. I repeat, for the price! And in saying that, it’s actually a really great price. The box it came in was extremely well packed. In fact every single thing on it had its own bit of protection, which was awesome. The bike was 90% pre-assembled. There was very little to do other than attach the pedals, the handlebars, Finish attachment of the fenders, etc. The typical stuff you’d usually expect. Batteries came about 60% charged. Of course I plugged it in and tried it out anyways to make sure it worked, and of course it did. Before my first ride I charged up both batteries to 100% using the included chargers, which didn’t take as long as I expected. Now the manufacturer states that it will get up to 28 mph and hold that speed on flat ground with an average load. I can confirm that this is true. The initial torque is actually quite good, and once you hit about 20 to 22 mph, obviously that torque wears down a bit. Assuming you’re on a flat surface, and not carrying anything on top of you or behind you, it will actually get to 28 (eventually). The motor does make some interesting noise when it’s floating at full speed, but no big deal. On the plus side, you can actually get this up to 30 mph with some small changes to the P settings.  Again, it won’t accelerate to that speed instantly. This particular motor and controller is set up to put out more torque than speed. As far as the range goes, I was able to get exactly 40 miles off of one full charge, and I suspect it could’ve gone at least another 10-12 if not more. I was doing a lot of stop & go which was super annoying lol, but not the bikes fault. The bike got a ton of looks everywhere I took it. Everybody who sees it is very interested it. It’s such a unique and striking design. Of course that’s one of the things that sold me on it, on top of the other positive points. I should also note that the “pedal assist” is more of a side effect than an actual function. The supplied gearing is VERY low. I never once took it out of seventh gear which is the top of the range for this model. Seventh gear even at a high cadence will take you to about 10 mph max. After that, you’re on electric only. On the other hand, it does give you a way to pedal the bike in a slow crowd should you decide not to use the throttle, or to pedal home if you simply went too far. The brakes feel pretty good, and I love the fact that it comes with hydros as stock. Not too many bikes at this price range have that (if any). As for comfort: For me I found that flipping the handlebar stem upside down made for a better riding position, but to each their own.  If in the future I’m looking for another rigid fat tire electric bike, I will certainly purchase another.

title: This is a really cool towel!
text:
Summer is on its way, and it's going to be a hot one! My husband is an electrician, and there generally is no power to run air-conditioning his job sites. Last year we attempted to keep him cool with coolers full of water and Gatorade. This year he wanted something more. Something that would really help lower his body temperature.
This cooling towel is just that thing. This towel is amazing, I have never felt anything like it before. Even without being wet this towel is cool to the touch. It's even cooler with the water! Not only did it keep him cool, it was long enough to wrap around his face to keep dust out. When he got home from work I threw the towel in with the basket of laundry, I was about to throw in the wash. The towel came out perfect. text:
I bought this bag in which to carry my lunch (breakfast and several snacks, too), as I'm a long way from home...often for twelve hours at a time. This bag is sturdy, the seams are strong, and the plastic is thick and durable. Most notably, it holds up extremely well despite many abuses throughout the day (vanpool, desk, placed on the floor, etc).

I'm impressed, too, by how essentially watertight this bag is. Not too long ago, I placed a bottled drink in the bag, only to find that I'd not tightly closed the lid. When I arrived to work, a large percentage of the drink was sloshing around in the bottom of the bag; yet, none of the liquid leaked out. Even as I walked the additional ten minutes to get to a bathroom (in order to clean out the bag), the liquid stayed inside the bag, and my clothes (and everything else) stayed clean and dry. As I looked inside, I discovered that the seams are double-bind/ double-sewn (yes, nice quality!).

title: First time using a hand grip strengthener and I must say... Its revolutionary.
text:
To summarize my review: This is a stress ball on steroids. If you ever feel stressed, this product will do wonders for you no matter how big, small, strong, or normal you are. This product will be integral to your daily life. It's highly adjustable and fits snugly no matter the hand size, and the grip is comfortable. Buy it.

Let me warn you: I am lazy. I hate standing, I hate moving, and I hate anything that requires any form of long-term physical discomfort. I do however love to work out, I love to walk on a treadmill at max incline, I love lifting weights, and I enjoy a good sweat and massage. So I understand this seems paradoxical but it's really not.

So imagine my surprise when I don't even have to get my big ass off the chair to get a good workout going!! No need for that rubber band, no need for barbells, no need for any form of effort beyond picking up some clickers and clicking them. It's easy, requires no preparation, and feels like lifting weights.

It has a counter, the counter is pretty bad. It isn't aligned properly, it only goes to 99, and resetting it is a pain. So I don't plan to use it. Also, the metal spring on it is perfect. It is made where you can change the position of the spring which increases the resistance up to 130 pounds. However... this is not exactly true.

I can easily max this out and do the 130-pound resistance however the problem is the thing starts to bend and the grip starts to move inwards and doesn't properly touch the other side causing the metal to bend. If you max this at 130 pounds for the long term, it will eventually bend and break. However, it's pure metal and it will take some effort to break. The grip is held against the spring by two large metal rods. So it's not like this product isn't very durable, it's durable.

If you are like me, lazy, unmotivated, and just wanted to workout because you enjoy the feeling, and love to pick something up and build strength, this is for you. The whole reason I bought it was that this was the best bang for your buck, there are 2 of them for 20$ and I don't like having to switch it between my hands. I am that lazy.

But, I do burn about 2000-3000 calories a week on the treadmill and other machines in the gym so this is a perfect little device for letting out a bit of energy while you are in your recovery period. I do wish it was capable of withstanding more than just 100 pounds but for me 100 pounds is perfect. I am 330 pounds with 24% bodyfat (around that.) and I can probably bench 350+. So trust me, if this works well for me, it will work extremely well for you.

2 Adaptable to warmer temps by not using mummy style or leaving baffle open.
3 Its plenty long to throw a water bottle warm in to keep feet toasty or if you were 6 foot plus you would fit nicely.

5 comfortable against skin
6 fluffs nicely for extra padding and extra length allows you to roll top for pillow if your not using as mummy.

title: Light weight emergency shovel
text:
This is a lightweight shovel with a telescoping handle. The shovel weighs 1.1 lbs. It has a thick aluminum blade and a textured plastic handle. The blade is 8.5” wide and 10.5” long. When completely telescoped, the total length of the shovel is 16.5” long. Fully unfolded, it is 30” long (including the blade). The telescoping handle has 3 spring-loaded buttons that release each section. The product was made in China.

I am quite impressed with the quality of this shovel. I like to carry a shovel in my car during winter for emergencies, like getting stuck in the inevitable snow bank. My old emergency shovel also had a telescoping handle, but the blade was plastic. Eventually, the plastic blade cracked and now there’s a big chip out of it. The handle on the old one also rusted from too much salt exposure. The blade on this shovel is much more heavy duty and it’s clearly not going to crack. The handle on this shovel also is coated, so I don’t think it will rust. What’s frustrating about this shovel, though, is that there are no stops on the telescoping action, so you can easily pull the handle right off the blade, or pull the sections of handle apart. So you have to pay attention when pulling the handle open not to pull too hard. As with any telescoping emergency shovel, the total length of this shovel is quite short, so you’re not going to want to shovel a driveway or sidewalk with it. But for clearing snow out from your car wheels, or getting out of a parking space after getting plowed in, this will do the trick.

title: GREAT PRODUCT and GREAT Customer Service
text:
I bought the Inflatable SUP May 2013 for my wife for our wedding anniversary and we have had so much fun enjoying the product I was compelled to write my first product review...even after 1 year has gone by. Frankly, this is one rugged / tough paddle board that continues to provide my wife and kids and their friends with a world of enjoyment. We just returned from 4 days at Lake Havasu and the board was in constant use with 2,3, and at times even 4 teens on it or hanging on it. Then when not is use is was lying on the rocky shore cooking in the 108 degree desert sun...yet when dragged back in the water it just kept on delivering a fun escape for my wife and daughters to paddle around and enjoy the serenity of the lakes back coves. I've lived in Arizona nearly all my life...it is very rare to encounter an inflatable product that can handle the heat, and we all agree this has truly been one of the best gifts I have given, and that makes this board a bargain at any price.

NOTE - This is not a silly inflatable pool toy...this is a real deal get out and use as often as time permits recreational marvel...yet it readily stows away...how can you beat that? 1 year of routine use and still going strong. But what really impressed me was the support I have received from Tower even thought I ordered from Amazon. I broke a small part on the pump and they shipped me a replacement and thanked me for enjoying their product. You don't come across that many Made In The USA manufacturers any more, and these guys are at the top. So for anyone who enjoys water, mild to mid level exercise, and FUN...this is the product and the company to work with. Period. Hope you find this review helpful. KCINAZ

title: Excellent value tent!
text:
This is the 8th tent that I currently own.
I have different tents for all occasions. From one person, uber lights, to 8 person, 4 season tents, I've pretty much got my bases covered.
The intention behind ordering this one was to replace the super-budget, 6lb, 2-3 person dome tent that my daughter likes to take when she goes tent camping, (we usually hammock, but there are times when we have to use tents).
She doesn't like the confined space of a one person tent like I use, so she's willing to pack a bit of extra weight for the increased living space.
At a tad under 4 lbs total weight for this tent, she's shaved 2+ lbs off of her already heavy base weight...nice.
The tent is 'mostly' free-standing. Which means that it doesn't have to be staked out to be fully functional. This is important if you are setting up on solid rock or even loose sand. I say 'mostly', because you do need to stake out the sides to get the maximum square footage, but it's not critical if you don't.
The rain fly is excellent and covers the entire tent, also providing a good sized vestibule to store gear or cook in during inclement weather.
If you are 100% sure you're not going to encounter rain, you can leave the fly at home, saving an additional 1.5 lbs of weight and still have a bug-free, albeit less private sleeping area.
All seams on the fly and bathtub floor are taped and showed no signs of leaking on the one night of rain she's spent in it so far.
As with any tent in humid weather, expect some degree of condensation. Because this is a two wall tent though, (separate body and rain fly), that is mitigated somewhat.
Overall I'm quite impressed with this tent.
For the price I think it really can't be beat.
You can spend 3-6× as much for a lighter, name brand option, but for the budget minded or a beginner who isn't exactly sure what they're going to need, this is an excellent option.
Very highly recommended.

title: better than buying EOTech
text:
I have an EOTech 517 mounted on my AR and I wanted a magnifier for it, but EOTech magnifiers cost more than the holographic sights! They can range between $500-600. This magnifier is virtually the same thing, except it has a higher zoom (7x vs 3x), so it is actually BETTER than the EOTech magnifier, yet you're only paying 1/5 the price for it. You can make your own decision, but I'm not paying $400 just to have the EOTech name printed on the side.

I don't seem to have a problem with the back focus, and I have 20/20 vision as well. In fact, I didn't even know I could adjust the focus on it (so the lens was in the forward-most position), and I was still able to use is just fine, as long as the target was 30yds or farther. Now that I know you can adjust the focus (the lens is now in the rear-most position), I can easily see targets 10yds away and I don't even have to focus my eye when looking at targets 30yds+, and lets be honest, you're not going to be shooting at targets that close with a 7x zoom anyway. I guess my point is that even if the back focus doesn't work 100% for you, you can still focus with your eyes.

My only gripe is that you cannot adjust it, so it may not line up perfectly with your reticle, but I don't think you can adjust EOTech's either.

I've been looking at a bunch of different ab wheels for a long time. No matter how much I exercise, my stomach sticks out. I want it gone. When I suck in my stomach and stand up a little straighter, I can see that I'm 1,000 crunches and a 24hr plank away from a cute little 6 pack. My waist is visible again; who knew I even had one? Anyway, the point is that my stomach isn't ideally as flat as I want it to be, but I've been looking all over for the right ab wheel to fix that. I don't have time for abdominal exercises that are going to tire out my arms and legs before I can even "feel the burn" in my stomach. Those suck. This ab wheel does not.

The wheel came in the box with the handles separated and wrapped in plastic. You have to install the handles into the wheel, and YES, it matters which handle goes in which side. The handles have those little silver buttons you have to push in so they can slide into the wheel. Those little buttons secure it, so I'm not at all worried about how long the handles are going to stay attached. I didn't hurt myself while inserting the handles but I came pretty close to it. Watch out for those silver buttons!

After putting it together, I tested it out. This was about 2-3hrs before my regular Crossfit training session. I Googled instructional videos and looked at the guy on the box. I know now that the first time I did it, I was doing it wrong, but apparently that didn't mean I wasn't going to be sore after. It felt like someone kicked me directly between my ribs that same day and the 3 that followed. I couldn't even laugh during those 3 days! "Ow," is an understatement.

Now that I'm doing it right, I'm probably abusing it. I want a flat tummy NOW!! After every session with it I'm looking in the mirror to see if something changed. Soon I'll be using a neoprene waist slimmer to enhance my results. I have faith in you, ab wheel, don't let me down.

text:
Everyone who is complaining about discoloration on the handles has failed to understand that the black color features a gray pattern. As for complaints about the handles becoming unscrewed mid-workout, I haven't experienced the same problem. It's always a good idea to do a quick safety check of any of the equipment you use prior to a workout, but both ends of the handles have remained as tight as they were the day I fastened them.

I didn't buy these for any specific workout routine. The real intent was to get some extra cardio in while I was working in an office that doesn't have enough room for a corded jump rope. It's pretty quick to catch on to the concept; if you've ever jumped rope, this will probably make sense to you almost immediately. It may seem a little weird at first, but it's a lot less strange than just jumping up and down in your office.

The weights in the handle add a nice feel, and I can't imagine using them without the weights. I'm not the most fit guy, but I don't find the weight to be unwieldy, and they don't make the workout unnecessarily arduous. You can remove them, but you probably won't.

If you have a young child, they will most likely (by which I mean absolutely) see this is as a potential toy (by which I mean weapon). And while you're unlikely to hurt yourself using them, your child will absolutely find a way to hurt you, hurt themselves, or hurt someone else when they flail it around. title: Stealth Cam G42 Review
text:
Have been using Stealth Cam cameras since they first became available, many years ago. The G42 is a quality camera (I believe released in 2000) and certainly far removed from some of the earlier models. Small, compact, well made camera. Picture resolution excellent and no issues during first month in the field. Sounds like battery life will be much longer than in the past, though I use external battery packs (with solar chargers) on all of my cameras. That raises the one con in my mind. The face screen completely shuts off after setup and it appears that the camera needs to be shut off and turned back on to see how many pictures are on the disk. I'm certain that this is a battery saver, but is somewhat inconvenient. Liked the camera enough though, that I promptly purchased two more. My cameras remain in the field 24/7 for as long as they function. Will provide and update in a year or so! Only wish that not everyone is only making IR models these days. The flash is nice for quality nighttime pictures and has no detectable effect on animals coming to a food source. This camera would be incredible for me, if it was flash!!
This is an update at the nine month point. Have multiple G42s in the field, both in the heat of Texas and the NE weather of Pennsylvania. All have worked flawlessly and I have purchased more. The most remarkable points in these new cameras by Stealthcam are the reliability and the battery savings. With the external battery packs and solar chargers it appears that I can go for months without a battery change out. We were always changing out batteries frequently, during the cold winter months in the NE. We went entirely through last winter and now well into the Spring without changing a battery!
UPDATE: These cameras have been in the field 24/7 for over two years now and have worked flawlessly. I have not had a single failure and have about a dozen of these cameras. I average about 60,000 pictures per camera, per year (one minute recycling tine), so these cameras have been excellent. I've been so impressed that I've just upgraded my review to five stars. Just ordered two more today at Amazon sale price to keep in reserve. Great camera!! Now if they would only make a similar model with flash, so that I could get great, night time pictures.
Update (2018): These cameras have now been in the field 24/7/365 for over four years and I have not had a single failure. Two cameras in PA were ripped off the trees to which they were mounted, by interested black bear, but each were placed back up and worked just fine. Here in Texas the mounting strap broke after being out in the sun for four years, but the camera is fine. Have 8 cameras in reserve but haven't needed any of them. Very solid product.
Update (2019): These cameras have been in the field 24/7/365 for over fifteen years (averaging 100,000+ pictures per camera, per year) and there have been no failures. Superb trail camera.
Update (March 2020): Read above as all still accurate. These cameras have been in the Texas heat and Pennsylvania cold for years 24/7/365. Not a single failure and hundreds of thousands pictures per camera. I have many cameras out in the field and many in reserve which I have never had to use. For me a definite 5 star camera.

title: AMAZING rings and straps for the cost!
text:
I use these in my home-gym and looped them around my squat rack's built-in pull-up bar rather than mounting them to the ceiling. The straps don't slide up and down or give at all. They feel very sturdy and high quality and they also look nice.

Tip: The metal rings have hundreds/thousands of tiny little metal pellets inside of them and they also have a small hole on one side that those pellets can be dumped out from. Open the ring's packaging outside or over a garbage can so the shower of metal pellets doesn't get all over your floor. Then shake the rings out with the whole facing down to get all the remaining pellets out of each of them.

Three things I'd change about the rings/straps, but not big enough issues to remove a star (they really are great!):

1) The straps aren't numbered so setting them up to be equal heights takes a little eyeballing and a tiny bit longer to adjust them. However, the positive trade-off is that they look a lot nicer without the big bright ugly numbers on them that some other brands have. If I could make one change though, it would be the addition of small subtle colored numbers (like dark grey). You only need to see the numbers when you're adjusting them they don't need to be seen from across the room or gym the competitor brands make them.

2) The excess strap material could really use some sort of management system. I flop it over the top of my pull-up bar they are hanging on or take a binder clip and clip the excess to another part of the straps. Maybe another carabiner specifically to pin the excess up? Or a small velcro ring or something could come with them.

3) For a first-time Olympic Ring newbie, like myself, it would have been really nice to include installation instructions/tips for both ceiling mount and looping them around something like a pull-up bar. It took a lot longer than expected to figure out the best way to loop them.

Minor issues, but I'd be willing to re-purchase these to get these three improvements if a new and improved version were released.

title: The perfect chicken / poultry feeder !!!!!
text: I bought this to replace a 30 lb hanging feeder because my girls were making a mess and wasting so much food by spilling it all over their run. Amazon shipping was fast and assembly of the unit was easy. I had this assembled, filled and up and running within half an hour. It went quick using this method and no sore fingers. I put in three 50 lb bags of layer pellets and still had room for a couple more bags. I set the timer for 2 drops, one at 7am and one at 6pm for 4 seconds each. I ran a test run and layer pellets flew out at least 10 feet in every direction. This was not good for me, since my run is only 8 foot wide, so I took the metal body of the hanging feeder and bungee corded it in place around the spinner motor. Now the feed drops straight down perfectly and makes a wonderful clanging noise when the feed shoots out to let everyone know dinner is served! You could also cut the btm out of a 5 gallon bucket and use the bucket for a drop tube as well. My girls love it. I have completely eliminated my feed waste and do not go through any unused feed now since it is all being eaten. Once I saw how well this worked I immediately ordered a 2nd unit for my other coop. I have no problems with squirrels or other varmints getting to the feed, so these should last a very long time. My next purchase will be the solar panels. I had one instance with caking, but this may have been due to damp feed I put in, because it hasn't happened since. I would give these 10 stars if I could. Forget rolling it up, just jam it in the bag, it will fit.  For car camping, sleep-overs at a friends house, or sleeping on the floor of your church with a bunch of high schoolers, this bag cannot be beat. I finished a short 20 minute test ride and noticed my butt was a little sore so I ordered a gel cushion today. I'm sure I'll continue to tweek things.

title: Good Quality, Good Value, Versatile Widths
text:
I bought this to put on my forthcoming tracklocross bike, but it's on my commuter bike now, and will probably remain. Well, it's lightweight, comfortable, durable, and it doesn't mark my pants. I was using Brooks saddles, but they are (relatively) heavy and they mark up my sit area with oil or scuffs (the cambium ones have a denim cover that scuffs my pants). I also appreciate the understated logo graphics.

I don't like to wear bike shorts except on long rides, and I don't care for any kind of gel or memory foam. The closed cell EVA foam on this saddle is comfortable, and there is also some spring from the large-ish gap between the rails and the seat. I mean, on my 3 mile commute I don't notice the saddle at all, can't say about longer bumpier rides yet. I'm 6 ft, about 160 lbs, and don't usually have much weight on the saddle.

So, I was unable to find many good reviews or descriptions on the Pro line of saddles, but I will try to give my advice based on what I could piece together. The "offroad" line has two other models; the Griffon and the Volture. This one, the Turnix is for moderately flexible riders, the Griffon is for less flexible, or more upright riding, and the Volture is for longer seated riding on an ebike. Additionally, there are 3 widths, the wider being theoretically more comfortable for more upright posture. Therefore, the 142 width will probably be most likely to fit most people if you don't have a known width preference. These have kind of a longer nose length more similar to a road saddle compared to the downhill MTB saddles. They have hollow stainless rails which I'm confident won't break on me. Pro makes some road saddles with carbon rails if you want to take a chance and shave some weight. Some reviews have complained that it's "slippery" but in my opinion if feels a bit sticky due to the rubberized details with my regular street clothes. I have to unweight to move around on the saddle.

These are manufactured by Shimano if you didn't know. My feeling is, while these are very well designed, Shimano is in the process of designing the "perfect" balance of weight, shock absorption, comfort, style, and practicality or function and durability. I think they nailed it, but there seems to be some previous versions still available here on Amazon. Most likely you can find something comparable from other name-brands at a similar price point too, probably also in the process of ongoing design. This saddle has a somewhat old school vibe which I like.

On Amazon, you will see a lot of 25 dollar saddles that look great in the thumbnail, but if you can imagine producing a good quality bike saddle for $25, you can probably also imagine the difference in finish quality and durability. In my opinion, the Pro line is a very good value for the price. (I bought a couple of the cheap seats on the 'Bay; they are lightweight and you can sit on them, but they are noticeably crappy and less comfortable.

One last thing is there is a mount on the bottom of the seat for Pro-line of saddle accessories, but unfortunately they don't make anything useful to me at the moment; just a go-pro mount, and like a CO2 mount, and a plastic ass-saver thingie. Still, I might try to rig something with a bit of aluminum to mount there.

TLDR; I'm very happy with this purchase. I'm ordering a Griffon model in 142 for comparison, and will use one for the commuter and one for the tracklocross (which will probably also be a commuter.)

title: This machine is so good, it hurts!
text:
[[VIDEOID:815fa207922ce396162c4d0c24e4614d]]

As a precautionary measure, I still wouldn’t or can’t go to the gym due to the pandemic situation, but I need to exercise at home too. It was hard for me to look for a machine that can give me a good cardio exercise, and yet compact enough to store and not an eye sore in a room. This machine is the smallest I can find that will suit my needs. I wasn’t disappointed.

I was excited when I saw the box as it is indeed small enough to hide under a bed. Out of the box, there is very minimal assembly needed, you just need to attach the pedometer at one of the steps, and the resistance bands to the base footing. I was already using this machine in less than 2 minutes. The steps have a good resistance to it and you can feel the burn on your legs up to your glutes in just 15 minutes. Using the resistance bands, you can target different muscle groups if you are creative. So far, I use it for bicep curls, front lateral raise, side lateral raise, and reverse flyes. There are more resistance bands out here in Amazon if you wish to use a stronger resistance band. I wasn’t expecting much from this machine until I did a full 30-minute cardio exercise. I used my Apple watch to track my burned calories, and in comparison to the stair master I use at the gym, this machine can elevate my heart rate higher, and have burned almost twice the calories for the same time. I jog every day, but I can still feel my legs get sore after using this machine. You can try to lean forward, backward, or try different angles of your body to target different muscle area of your legs up to your glutes. Honestly, I love how this machine can give me a burn.

Some reviewers are complaining about squeaking sounds, I also noticed that on the very first day. I was able to isolate where the squeak is coming from, it was from the bolt connected to the step and pulley ties (see picture attached). I just put a little drop of WD-40, and everything is nice and quiet. I can exercise inside our room while my wife is asleep.

Overall, I am very impressed how this machine can give me a good workout. If you are like me who would like to exercise at home, then this compact machine is a very good option.

I've fished Daiwa products for more than 30 years, and they've always been my go-to brand. Now, I'm not so thrilled anymore.

The fit and finish overall is very nice, and the bearings make both the casting rotation and the retrieve glass-smooth. The magforce brake has 10 positions allowing almost infinite adjustability. The oversize handles and the offset crank provide easy operation.

This reel could have been great, but instead all the nice features that Daiwa incorporated into it are wasted on just another plastic-framed Wal-Mart-quality reel. If they'd have only actually made it with an aluminum frame, even at a higher price point, it would have dominated the sub-$200 market. But, that was not to be. I sent it back and bought a Quantum Kinetic PT, which actually does have an aluminum frame. The Quantum doesn't have nearly as nice features as the Daiwa - but it's rock solid with no flex or distortion whatsoever.

title: Consider the batteries non-changeable. Wish I did.
text:
Tl, dr: While the small size and brightness was promising, the near impossibility of battery replacement makes them effectively disposable. I can't realistically recommend.
===
I received this item (4 light version) as a gift from a relative who ordered them via Amazon in late May 2022. Since I don't have access to their account to give a "Verified Purchase" review, I am writing it here on my personal account. My review reflects 3 months of not-quite daily use.
At first, I thought these were a great deal for $11. Each unit came with batteries preinstalled, the light it emitted was surprisingly bright and the small button to cycle through 4 light modes -- off, fast blink, slow blink, steady -- was easy enough to press.
The problems started when I needed to change the batteries, which happened around 15-20 hours of using various light modes. The light dimmed in linear fashion starting around 8 hours and by the end were not bright enough to see even at arm's length.
Including the extra CR2032 batteries & two small screwdrivers was nice, but not so nice was how the first light became inoperable after changing the batteries. No configuration of up/down with the batteries would work. Tried about 10 times to make it work, screwing down 4 tiny screws each time, then gave up.
The 2nd battery change actually worked.
The 3rd did not.
So I now have 2 dead lights and 2 that are on their last legs in terms of lighting power. I don't have much confidence in the impending battery changes. It's up to you to decide whether $11 is a good price for (probably) one-use lights.
As someone who read the reviews and made a gift request based on those recommendations, I wanted to relate my experiences. Good luck.

title: UCO forces customers to do their quality control
text:
UPDATE:

After returning the lantern discussed below as defective, I received a replacement which suffers from the same manufacturing sloppiness as the prior one, but only slightly less bad: At least the sticker was on straight. The wobbly candle jacket—still there. The wobbly base—still there. And on the replacement, the bail (which on the 2015 original fits snugly around the collapsed lantern) is almost comically large and flops around when the lantern is collapsed, making the act of inserting the lantern into the closed-cell foam "cocoon" unnecessarily arduous and fumbly.

"Slightly less bad" is a low bar to clear and nowhere near a resounding endorsement. The single star still stands, and I stand by my assessment that UCO have long since fired their entire quality assurance staff and replaced them with a chronically damp salt shaker glued to the seat of a wobbly three-legged stool located in a completely different hemisphere from their manufacturing operations.

ORIGINAL REVIEW:

I have an UCO brass candle lantern from 2015. Its parts fit together perfectly with no play, and it has logged hundreds of hours of burn time with both paraffin and beeswax candles, with no drips, no smokiness, and a pleasing patina developing on the brass.

Then, in August of 2022, I purchased this brass UCO lantern again. There is a world of difference. And not in a good way.

When I received the lantern, the gold-colored aluminum jacket that holds the candle wobbled back and forth, because it did not seat properly in the base—the flared edges were flared too much.

The base itself also wobbled, because the indentations at the bottom of the brass body were too small and shallow to seat properly in the threads on the outside of the base (it's actually miraculous that the glass chimney survived shipping, as the candle wobbles so much that the metal jacket hits the glass with a minor shake of the lantern when both open and closed).

To add insult to injury, the "original UCO candle lantern - Estd. '71" sticker on the outside of the lantern isn't even applied straight ... there's a noticeable slant to it, and it's off center.

For the price we pay, I expect something significantly closer to perfect than this miserable excuse for a "trusted, time-tested lantern". As a minimum bar, I don't expect to have to make adjustments to parts to get them to fit properly.

I understand that UCO changed the location where these lanterns are manufactured in 2019. They also appear to have changed the location where they inspect them for quality—from "somewhere, anywhere at all" to "nowhere".

Honestly, I have no earthly idea why UCO charges us more for these now than 7 years ago when I bought the first one—they should be paying us for detecting these defects on their behalf!

UCO, if you're listening, your quality has hit a new low point, and you're damaging your reputation.

Read to the End:
Initial Review: I have to say I'm pretty impressed with this tent! Aluminum poles provide extra support although upgraded stakes would have been nice. The footprint/floor seems almost rubberlike and seems were taped for a nice seal. I did not put a tarp underneath which usually is a big no no for me, I also left both vents open. I used a thermarest r rated pad with a wool blanket folded over under me as my bed and a sleeping bag rated for 20 deg. I slept great! Probably the best night sleep in a tent I've ever had! By morning I had to open the front and back zip doors because it was toasty. Easily cooled down!

UPDATE: The next day we set up my Ole Reliable 15 year old Ozark Trail 4 person tent. We ended up with 25 mph gusts and Ole Reliable caved in but this Flytop tent hasn't budged! Will wait til winter before rating at 5 stars but looks promising!

UPDATE 2:
Last night we had scattered showers with a short period of medium strength heavier rain. I went out to sleep in the tent to check seems and was pretty disappointed because I did not expect to see leakage. The outside rainfly was leaking at the seam where you can roll up/tie the front vestibule, dripped right onto the inner tent door netting and onto my sleep pad because I didn't have the inner liner zipped on that side of the tent. The rain was beaded up on the outside of the rainfly and looked promising. The leaking happened on both sides even though the seams looked like they had tape along the seams on the inside. I did sleep in the tent the rest of the night but only because it didn't rain anymore. I don't see this being a 3-4 season tent if it can't handle a little rain. All I can say is that I wasn't expecting leakage during a calmer short lived rain...glad I hadn't trekked out with it yet. Will be returning.

I will update this review if and when ICON Fitness handles my issue to my satisfaction, but as of now I have my doubts if this will happen. I have a NordicTrack 1750 Commercial Treadmill, which I love, so it is really painful for me to create a 1-star review for this S22i. The build quality on the machine I received is terrible. The entire body of the machine leans over to the left and is out of alignment with the seat. The pictures attached barely does justice to the issues, but believe me, in person it is really obvious to the eye, let alone when sitting on the bike. The handlebar unit when attached is out of alignment, and even the NordicTrack logo on the main monitor is so crooked / skewed over that it should be an embarrassment to ICON Fitness and the NordicTrack brand. I want to remain an enthusiastic NordicTrack and ICON Fitness (iFit) customer but dealing with customer service thus far has been painful. I've explained in detail what my issues are, as well as sent them the pictures associated with this review, but they are only addressing the issue of the poorly manufactured handlebar. If you are buying this machine, be sure to carefully check the unit you receive for quality issues like these. The demand for exercise machines during the pandemic has been through the roof, which I'm sure has companies like NordicTrack rushing as many orders as they can through outsourced manufacturers ... it's the most likely hypothesis I can come up with that explains how a company known for high quality products, like NordicTrack, could send their customers such junk. Check back for an updated review if I ever get a working machine. Fingers crossed.

title: NOT worth the money
text:
First off: I generally don't write a review on anything until I've broken it. Anyone can tell you about the packaging or their YouTube unpacking, but in order to speak with any sort of authority on a product, you need to have spent enough time with it to have pushed it passed it's limits.

The Hyperion has been with me on a half dozen trips now, and half of those were absolute catastrophes.
The bag is fine, provided you camp in a laboratory. I do not. Most of what I do is primitive, at best. The type of camping where your ground pad is a bag filled with stripped fir boughs. The times I've used it in a tent, with modern ground insulation, during fair weather, it's been fine... No complaints. But this last weekend I had my third major freeze with it.

The first, my lean-to took on snow during a mountain storm, which got the bag slightly damp. It was like sleeping on a sheet of ice. It was also up off the ground, on a cot, so not just regular old negligence.

The second time, also in Montana in the Little Belts, we had a drop in temp to around freezing. The bag alone was NOT enough to keep me warm. This was within it's published "comfort range", and I found it to be unacceptable. Keep in mind that I'm not expecting a 5-star resort, here. I just expect to be warm enough to actually sleep.

This final time was in the Ozarks. The bag was again dry, but utterly insufficient to stay warm in the 32-40 degree range. I'm floored by this, as I bought this bag anticipating my longstanding hope of finding a bag that was easily portable, lightweight, and sufficiently warm was answered. I've been storing it correctly (in the large storage sack, not the compression sack) when not in use. I've used ground pads, cots, hammocks, and the bare ground itself, and have only been comfortable when inside a tent or rooftop tent.

I hate to write this review. If I'm doing something wrong, I'd love to know it so I can get back to believing this bag is what I hoped it could be. But at this point, I feel like I just pitched $450 into a frozen cat hole.

title: I strongly recommend you seeing before buying it online
text:
I’ve been aware of these products for about eight years, I’ve never seen one in person but the amount of reviews over that time on YouTube from people I follow has been quite a few. The products looked to be good and I finally found myself buying one of their hip-bags.

I’ve been carrying a shoulder bag for thirty years out of necessity and some have been with me for years at a time but none of them stay in place in any sense of the word as this Maxpedition , if I elect to use the belt this thing is not going anywhere!

The bag + shipping to the Middle East + customs= $200 so needless to say my expectations were running high.
I open the bag that it was shipped in and it was the wrong color. The paperwork correctly stated ‘khaki’ but the bag was military olive drab green. So that mistake made that bag unusable for me.
But pressing on to the functionality of the bag. The gap between what I was expecting and what I was holding was fairly vast. Now I mentioned it sits well- five stars for that.
The first and foremost problem that should have been remedied is the waist strap. My waist is 42” and with some effort I can get it closed and it’s a nice feature if you’re concerned that someone is going to try and yank it away from you. But the part that is an epic fail is when you disconnect it and you no longer want to use it. This feature fails because at this point you either have to totally disconnect both ends of the belt—no easy task—or play with the thing for a good few minutes to shrink it down so that it isn’t showing and hanging about to look stupid and more importantly catch on things.

Another thing that I didn’t like about this bag were the compartments, they are in my opinion very specialized and if they don’t meet your needs exactly you’re carrying a lot of dead space. I’ll give you some examples of what I mean.
To start with you have two pouches that are constructed well but they are limited as to what you can put in them. If I take my Leatherman Super Tool 300 out of its carrying case it fits well but it is not ideal for care of that tool . Some cans of pepper spray will fit others will not and I personally don’t carry it. A flash light would fit but I’m not so sure I would trust a $100-$150 flashlight to these pockets, a cheap one yes but not a good one.
Next we have the flap, I’ve got nothing to say about the Velcro that’s for sheer silly business. The pocket would be fine for an ID or some loose change a chap stick but nothing significant.
The main compartment has this draw string “storm lid” and I can’t really see what the point of this thing is. It gives another good four inches of height but if you do so it doesn’t close with the flap! If you leave it tucked it you’ve got to wonder “what were they thinking?” When this storm shield is resting inside of the bag it is totally in the way of using the two side pockets that are on either side. I chose to place my flip wallet and my credentials here rather than on the outer pocket, what a pain it is to get the thing out. So at the moment I have those items and two notebooks inside one is 1/8” thick the other is 1/4 “thick . For all practical purposes my main compartment is full…for me I am going to need to take out this storm collar if it is ever to be used in any meaningful way.

Now we get to the space that they have a lot to answer for and that is the space they recommend for a concealed weapon. I’ve just told the few items I have in that central part of the pack --- it is nowhere near stuffed in the least and yet everything there encroaches on this space for CCW. The smallest gun that I have is a .380 and if I were to put it in there I’d have a dickens of a time getting it out. With a case that Velcros inside that would be damn impossible without leaving the center compartment empty. To give you some idea on just how tight this thing is I wanted to put my eye glass case in there last night it measures 6”x2.5”x1” and it requires finagling. Who wants to go through that just to get to their glasses?

I’m not going to speak on some of the ridiculous things that Maxpedition suggests to say nothing of some of the goofs on Youtube when they talk about lashing things under the pack with the generous space provided. This isn’t a rucksack people, you’re going to put your bed roll underneath!
Another thing that needs to be modified is the handle. Come on guys a nice rubberized grip or something of the sort didn’t cross your minds in the design process? You can doctor it up with a paracord handle if you’ve got the know-how but really it should be done for you at the factory.

The side pocket is currently storing the belt from swinging about, if I put something in there then I have nowhere to store the belt, as I already mentioned there should have been considerable attention given to this idea before production.

The most important fail on my trial with this bag is carrying it. As a professional tour guide this bag is on me off and on through a ten hour day and my neck and shoulder are so raw from the strap cutting into me it’s impossible to use as it is intended as a daily bag. Besides the actual weight of the bag I have no more than ten ounces in it with credit cards, ID a flash light and some pills. It’s ridiculous to think of adding even more lash ons to put more stuff, it simply can’t hold that weight and be comfortable.

Last but not least is the Sound Meter reading. If you’re a grunt, or in a tactical position where low noise is essential then you will want to know that the read out comes out to 80 decibels on the largest zipper which is equivalent to a busy street or alarm clock. The buckles and smaller zipper are in the mid 50’s

I would recommend seeing this bag before buying it making sure this is going to be a good fit for your needs. For a bag that’s made in Taiwan I’ve got to wonder what production cost is and how much profit there is in each bag. I would expect a price tag to the consumer to range between $30-$40 beyond that it’s hard to justify the cost.

title: This survival kit needs some upgrades.
text:
There is a saying “Prepare for the worst, hope for the best.” I would hope that I would never need to find out if I could survive in a wilderness environment but you never know. I saw this survival kit and asked Amazon to review it.

I have experience in the wilderness, but I always had an idea of what I was facing. I have backpacked in most of the Western United States, Alaska, and Canada. My longest trip was in the Wind River Range in Wyoming. It was harsh, beautiful, high terrain, and at night it could get cold. I have helped rescue people who were not prepared. It’s amazing what people think they can do without the proper equipment.

Different people will evaluate this kit differently based on their experience or lack thereof, their abilities, and their knowledge of the subject. I have met people who would tell you this kit would be more than adequate, and it might be for them. I am just writing this review based on my experience and what I think my abilities are.

Several years ago I took a wilderness survival class as part of an overall series on the out-of-doors. I am not a survivalist, but I want to survive if something bad happens. They taught me that you need to set your priorities when finding yourself lost in the wilderness. They gave us “the rule of twos.” First, within the first 2 minutes assess yourself for injuries. If you have some take care of them immediately. Second, within the first 2 hours find or make a shelter. You need to stay dry and/or warm. Third, within the first 2 days, you need to find water. Fourth, within the first 2 weeks, you need to find food. You can live a long time without food. I thought using this rule would be a good way of judging a survival kit.

FIRST AID: I would give this kit a C-. It has a number of deficiencies. I will list a few. 1. It doesn’t have enough large bandages for large wounds. 2. The scissors are horrible. They will not cut most things I tried them on, including the bandage material included. 3. They give you about 100 Q-tips. In the many years I have backpacked, I have never had a need for a Q-tip. You don’t want things you are unlikely to use. 4. They have plastic tweezers. They don’t work well at pulling out small things from your skin. You need a good pair of metal tweezers.

MAKING A SHELTER AND STAYING DRY: Here I would give this kit a C. It has a number of things that would be helpful in making a shelter. However, the entrenching tool that is advertised is way too small to dig any kind of hole within a reasonable time limit. The ax is very small. It is sharp and will cut a 1 ½ inch branch but it takes a lot of time. It has a number of saws. The cable saw works best on dry wood. I tried it on a living branch and got nowhere. It provides a poncho and a lightweight emergency blanket, which reflects heat back to your body. They will help you stay dry and/or warm. There is a sharp pocket knife that is large enough to be helpful.

WATER: Here I would give this kit a D. It has nothing to purify water. There are no filters or pills to kill bacteria. Both are inexpensive and lightweight. The reason I gave it some points is that the poncho and emergency blanket can collect water or water moisture. A problem is if you are collecting rainwater you need to decide which protective clothing you are going to use.

FOOD: Here I would give the kit a D+. It has a knife and a small packet with things to catch fish. It really isn’t very much. There are only 2 hooks. I thought they should have put a quantity of dry bait in the package. There is something that looks like a worm, but I'm guessing you are not going to catch a fish with it let alone survive. You could dig for worms but you're not going to survive on fish with only 2 hooks.

What I have outlined are my major concerns. There are more but I have tried to keep this to several pages. One of my overriding concerns is that there is no booklet telling you how to survive in the wilderness. It doesn’t tell you how to build a simple shelter or the best ways to get water when there is not a stream around or how to trap small animals. There should be a booklet that addresses the major problems you are going to face. They give you a fire starter and two things that are probably very flammable. I have seen experts start of fire with a spark, but it requires knowledge and a lot of practice. It is many times more difficult if things are wet. I think they should have included a lighter or at least some information on how to use the fire starter. There won't be any YouTube when you are trying to survive in the wilderness.

Finally, I can't emphasize enough the need to have a decent supply of duct tape in any survival kit. It can be used for so many things. It can be used for first aid, it can hold things together, it can repair tents, it can hold your shoes together, it can be used to repair tears in your clothing, you can use it as rope, and so many other things.
product_name: Survival Kits,222 PCS Emergency Survival Gear First Aid Kits with Molle System Compatible Bag Outdoor Camping Gear Emergency Kits for Hunting,Hiking,Fishing, Gifts for Men Women

title: Save your money for a better quality tent that won't fail on first use.
text:
Final Update~
The replacement tent they sent was a lesser model, and it was actually dirty and used..with sand and grit all over the inside. Still, I put it up in my back yard to see how it would do. It completed collapsed and filled with water, under modest wind and rain. Completely unnacceptable. Upon advising them of this situation and expressing my unhappiness at getting a lesser replacement tent that was used and dirty, they offered to refund my money and upgrade me to the Colorado 8/9 tent. Again, I was hopeful. However, upon first use, one of the poles is already splintered and the connecting shock cord broke.
Now, I've field tested three NTK tents~ Cherokee 8/9, the Oregon 8/9 and the Colorado 8/9 tent models. They have all three been of poor quality and failed upon their first use, in my back yard, under moderate, reasonable weather conditions. I can't imagine the disaster if I got caught in a storm in of of these flimsy mesh bags. In light of this, I'm now down to one star, and I'd encourage anyone looking at NTK to look elsewhere.
Update~ I contacted NTK directly. They immediately responded via their chat message option on their website. They offered to replace the tent, no charge to me. I understand QC sometimes misses a problem here and there, I am accepting their offer of replacement. Once I get the replacement and test it out, I'll revisit this review and update accordingly. I do very much appreciate how responsive their customer service has been, which also played into my decision to accept replacement rather than ask for a refund.

I tested this tent in my backyard over 3 days of steady wind and rain. I didn't sleep in it, just wanted to see how it woud hold up in the elements. I was happy to find that it handled the wind fine. A small pool of water gathered in one of the corners due to a weak stitching job on the corner loop. But, I kept the tent and hoped for the best.
I just got back from my first actual camp in the wilderness. I am sad and disappointed to report that the floor of the tent didn't hold up at all and now has mulitple holes, from dime-sized to smaller. I am an experienced camper. I've owned multiple tents of all styles and sizes over the years. I've never had a tent floor get holes like this. We keep our boots off and only use socks while walking in the tent. We utilized it exactly as it says it's designed for, as we have all our previous tents.
We used a sturdy tarp as a footprint, and the ground was covered in fallen leaves, so it had a fairly gentle pitch spot. Now that I've hung it up to air out, I'm noticing that all four corners have weak stitches and have already started to fray, after using this tent for two nights only.
The floor looks plenty sturdy, like it's made out of rugged tarp material. It is actually quite flimsy. Don't be fooled. It also is bowled and doesn't lay flat at all, whick makes it a constant snag and trip hazard.
The poles held up in the wind, but with the low quality issues I'm already having, I wouldn't be surprised if they break, too.
I do like the guyline system on the rain fly. The zippers worked great, without constant snagging. It is easy and fast to put up, but most folks will need another person to help. That's all the positives I have to say.
I'm past the return date, so I'm stuck with it. I'll be putting Tenacious Tape on the holes and try to fortify the fraying corner stitches as best I can. Most likely, I'll just continue to use my 6 person cabin tent and use this thing as an extra for friends to come along. I thought I was getting a good deal on a bargain tent that was made well enough to last 3-5 years of regular use. $200+ for a tent is only a good deal if the tent lasts more than one use before materials start failing. I'll start saving for the Big Agnes or the REI Kingdom today.

title: Flip lid can open
text:
I recently bought these at Costco last week. Same design, but the box is slightly different. Either way, its the same product, including even the colors. i've looked at the other Smart Source reviews and it seems that product has a different top, where you have to suck on it more, similar to a sports bottle cap. This lip just has a flip top on it, and its not that great. It clicks when you close it, but its not that sturdy. I had three of them filled up for a trip to a local theme park. I bought these because I have 2 other steel bottles that aren't insulated and without a sleeve and got tired at how quickly they warm up and leech on the outside. I had them in a bag and when I got off the shuttle from one park to the other, my son notices water on the floor from the bag. Sure enough, one lid flipped open and poured 80% of the water into my bag. Luckily, the bottles were the only thing in it.

the top can easily be opened, either accidentally or on purpose. There isn't much resistance when its "locked." If this had a sports bottle top, then it would be better. i'd rather have to work for my water, than have it spill out. I spent much of my line time checking to make sure they were all closed.

The neoprene also was a disappointment. As I stated, I had other bottles, but wanted these to keep the cold longer. That didn't really happen. I had these bottles in a bag in the bottom of a stroller and usually parked the stroller in the shade when I went on various rides. the water didn't last any significant time cooler than non-sleeved ones. I wager about 1 hour more, and then that wasn't even cold, but rather slightly cool. Not enough to make me jump for joy. My children's insulated steel Toy Story cup can hold water cold, not cool but COLD, for more than 24 hours. I'd have hoped the sleeve would keep mine cold for at least 6 hours. I even filled the water from our fridge and left the bottle in the fridge overnight. then I put the sleeve on before I left.

I will say, it held alot of water and the colors are nice. However, you do not see the colors if you have the sleeve, so that is a waste really. The other product says the sleeve loop isn't big enough for your finger, but this one is. Its also easy to get on. I fold the sleeve top over, like a pant cuff or a shirt cuff. Then I stretch it over the bottom of the bottle and pull up. works very easily. takes less than 10 seconds to get it on. The look on the top at the back of the cap can also fit your finger. Although when you flip the top open to drink, the lid gets stopped by that finger loop (top right of the picture) so you have to tilt your head back when you are low on water.

Could have been better designed. i'm going to return mine.

text:
I REALLY wanted to love this product. I golf 4-5 times/week and was excited to have my own swing analyst in my pocket. But this thing is total garbage and when combined with a horrendously complicated and unfriendly App, is basically unusable.

While the technology behind the GSA is very cool, this product should not be on the market. It is maybe at the end of Alpha testing, or beginning Beta at best. Here's why..

1) It doesnt come with a manual or user guide, just a cryptic quick start guide. The GSA website is no help either as its FAQ is even more generic

2) IT DOESNT HAVE AN ON/OFF SWITCH. There is a barely audible click when you push down really hard on the top, but is that the switch? There is no travel of the top so its not a button

3) Why won't the GSA pair with android consistently? I have 3 android devices running 3 different versions of android and none of them could consistently pair with the GSA. The "quick start guide" seems to indicate that it has to be plugged in to pair. Really? I have to plug in the GSA to a wall outlet just to pair it?

4) What do the stupid lights mean? It has red and blue lights that combine to form all kinds of "Close Encounters" style flashing patterns. But nowhere does it tell you what they mean

5) Which app do i use, pro or lite? I think lite is meant for android but why call it "lite"? Just friggin call it GSA Android. WTF?!?

title: Junk bearings
text:
This is my first time venturing away from Bones, and I regret it. These bearings have multiple areas that aren't good.
1) They fit way too loosely over the axles, the wheels have too much lateral play.
2) Despite installing them flush into the wheels, the bearings themselves seem crooked and the wheels have a solid wobble.
3) I get that bearings need to be broken in, but at least one wheel slows down to a stop real quick.
4) One makes a raggedy sound just like old dry/dirty bearings do. As if something in there is asymmetrical

Maybe these are just QC issues and maybe they usually have a good product, but each wheel has an issue and all the bearings just have different sounds and things going on, none of them are consistent. More importantly, the first two points can easily lead to uneven or excess wear on the trucks and wheels, and that's especially problematic.

Update: Just replaced these with Bones Reds. I examined them closer, the spacers were much wider than the gap in the wheel, so the bearings won't sit flush in the wheel. That gap between the wheel and bearing would've caused a lot of stress between the two bearing rings, increasing the risk of a dangerous bearing blow out. The bones have much thicker metal rings, they free spin much longer (the stingers slow quickly), and they have smaller ball bearings (less friction).

The Stingers also have really loose tolerances and a lot of play (which should be a really low ABEC rating). There's a lot of side-to side wiggle room between the two rings. You can kinda rattle them. There's machine marks on the ring side faces. The rings also have beveled edges (less surface contacting axle and wheel), and by spinning them, you can see the beveling is ever so slightly uneven on a few (the width of the outside ring surface changes). Spinning them and looking from the side, there's an uneven wobble you can see in some of the racers, and at least one seemed to have uneven thickness to the outer ring. Another one when rolled across glass had a jerky/rough spot in it's rotation. None of that indicates "precision", but it definitely indicates a possible injury if you're bombing a hill on these.

If you still decide to make this purchase, you might want to try requesting for multiple replacements and may be able to pick out one that you think it's best to keep :). For a $90+ ball, I expected more... Makes me wonder how this ball is considered a pro's game ball.

Good little light, but we're not getting 300 hours of light on the Low setting as stated in the advertisement. More like 30 hours. Thought it was too good to be true.

(We use these around the stables for nightlights for our old retired horses. We have four of them, two on the charger at home, and two in use. We swap them daily.)

UPDATE (23 Apr 2021):

Have 10 of these, and have been using them for about 1.5 years. Your mileage may vary.

We use them around the stables and in the trees to provide light at night for our old retired horses. Every day, we hang 5 freshly charged lights, and take down 5 to charge them.

THEY DO NOT PROVIDE LIGHT ON THE LOW SETTING FOR 300 HOURS AS STATED IN THE DESCRIPTION. They last only about 30 hours, and that is why each light gets changed to a freshly charged one daily.

THEY ARE NOT WATERPROOF. The lights collect rain water in the bottom of the globe. There is no way to open them to drain out the water and dry them. Any light with water is placed charging end down, and allowed to sit for a few days for any water to drain out. The light is then recharged and used as normal.

After about 1.5 years of daily use, the charging connector on several light has become fussy about charging. The connectors are loosening in the fixture, and the charging wire has to be wiggled to get it to charge.

These lights originally cost about $25 USD each. I am considering replacing them because of the charging problems. $25 for 1.5 years of useful life seems a little costly. I’m looking for a less expensive and longer term solution.

Of the original 10 that we bought less than 2 years ago, only 5 still work, and will accept a charge. Still only get about 30 hours on low setting. Am replacing them with a different light. Not worth the charging hassle, or expense of replacing every 18 months.

title: A Toy -- Not for Advanced Golfers
text:
I kinda suspected that as I tried the Phigolf Mobile Simulator that there was a good chance that, as a single-digit handicap golfer, I might be disappointed. I was. That's not to say it's not a fun "toy," but that is what it is. And one might consider getting a Nintendo Wii and have just as much fun and many more games in the process.

The Phigolf Swing Stick is convenient indoors, but it's absolutely not hitting a real ball. Nothing can replace that. And the Swing Stick certainly doesn't register whether I've heat a fat or thin shot. It barely represents even the most basic of swing parameters, like clubhead speed, swing path or face angle. In fact, the idea of a clubhead or a club face is purely in one's imagination!

But what if I put the sensor on a real club? Well, fine, but you'll quickly discover that it's not so accurate in its measurements. Being off by 10-20% is a lot! In fact, even the Quick Start Guide I received warned me that it wasn't intended to accurately reflect a real swing! I normally hit balls into a net at home, but the Phigolf sensor was ignoring (or not seeing) when I was obviously chunking a shot.

Then there is the short game. I am trying to be gracious here, but there is just no way to reproduce matter of touch when it comes to pitch shots, chip shots and putts. To me, this is where golfers score. But whatever touch I have learned in real life was simply not transferred to the game.

If you're new to golf or you don't expect to do anything more than doing something with friends while having a few beers, this might be for you. If you are a serious golfer, you may have to do gymnastics to try to suspend your expectations.

I returned my purchase. It's not for me.

title: Can't recommend it
text:
Just got it today. And there are so many things that are wrong with this bag.
First of all, the bag is VERY SMALL, even without a handgun in it. The key department is a joke (unless you have exactly one key). The front departments are barely big enough to put a wallet in (I actually had to go through my wallet to remove unnecessary stuff so it will fit).
Now to the gun sections. There are 2 big compartments, allegedly you can carry a handgun in both of them. However, you can't really carry in the middle compartment - if you have a wallet in the bag, it becomes so tight that you can't reliably draw from it! Also, there is no fast opening ring in it.
This leaves us with the rear compartment only. But it is barely big enough to accommodate even a mid size handgun (my VP9 fits, but it took me a while to fit it in so it won't interfere on opening). And forget about putting your handgun diagonally - if you carry a mid size gun, your only option is vertical.
That said, the opening of the rear compartment is not symmetrical, thus while the gun is held vertically, you are forced to draw diagonally - and good luck with that.
Now, if you are left-handed, forget about this bag - there is no convenient way for you to draw the gun. But even for a right-handed person, you need to hold the bag with your left hand, open the bag with your right hand (using the ring), and then to draw with your right hand - not the fastest way by any means. But the rear compartment is not symmetrical, so this is your only way.
The universal holster SUCK! It will catch on literally anything on the gun - extraction window, front post... I made it function somewhat reliable by attaching the holding strap diagonally and very loosely. However, now the trigger is semi-exposed, so i am not sure how safe my setup is.
I can't comment on the materials and durability yet, but everything seems to be cheap made, cheap thin materials and plastic.
I am going to give this bag a chance. If it holds up I will update this review. However, I would not buy it again.

I wore this for almost two years, now I'm writing a review. Bottom line: I got frustrated with two things that caused me to give this away and buy a Vivoactive HR (on which neither of these two problems occur).
